# FatalHandler

`Svc::FatalHandler` is an F' system-service component that receives fatal conditions and applies the deployment's terminal fatal-response policy. It is placed in the Level 4 system-control layer because its response is satellite-wide rather than specific to one hardware subsystem. F' provides the component documentation [here](https://fprime.jpl.nasa.gov/latest/Svc/FatalHandler/docs/sdd/).

## HuskySat-2 fatal-event ownership

Hardware managers remain responsible for detecting device-specific failures and reporting them through typed events. A hardware-related fatal event can carry a unique opcode identifying the affected hardware. The owning Level 3 application receives the fault, maps the opcode to the appropriate manager, and issues that manager's reset command. This preserves the App-Manager-Driver boundary: the application decides what recovery action is appropriate, the manager owns the device-specific reset sequence, and the driver only exposes the low-level interface.

`FatalHandler` should remain the final system-level path for unhandled or escalated fatal conditions. It does not replace a hardware manager or become a central hardware-reset owner. If an event cannot be mapped safely to an owning application or hardware opcode, the deployment can escalate it to `FatalHandler` according to the spacecraft fault-response policy.

## Proposed hardware-fault pipeline

The following is a proposed event and recovery flow. The exact event ports, opcode type, and escalation thresholds are TBA.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
    M["Hardware manager detects fault"] --> E["Hardware fatal event<br/>unique hardware opcode"]
    E --> EM["EventManager<br/>event routing and filtering"]
    EM --> A["Owning Level 3 application<br/>interprets opcode"]
    A --> C["Targeted reset command<br/>to selected manager"]
    C --> M
    E -. unhandled or escalated .-> F["Svc::FatalHandler<br/>system-level fatal response"]
```

This design keeps reset authority with the application-manager path while giving the system a defined terminal response when targeted recovery is unsafe or unavailable. The opcode namespace should be centrally documented so that every hardware manager emits unique, stable identifiers.
